local.h: Albany Park's Montrose Saloon to close after five decades
local.b: Montrose Saloon at 2933 W. Montrose Ave. will close after the new year, the bar announced Friday, ending a run of more than 50 years.
local.title: 'It's like our living room': Montrose Saloon in Albany Park set to close after decades-long run

local.h: Judge lets Illinois hemp THC ban take effect
local.b: Hemp-derived THC products can no longer be sold outside dispensaries in Illinois after a judge upheld the ban's original timeline, rejecting a challenge from businesses.
local.title: Judge denies pause on hemp THC product ban, prohibiting sale outside dispensaries

local.h: Could a redevelopment authority fix Cook County's vacant lots?
local.b: More than 100 Chicago leaders met in workshops on repurposing an estimated 50,000 vacant lots across Cook County, floating ideas from community farms to housing and a proposed redevelopment authority.
local.title: Could a redevelopment authority solve Cook County's vacant lot problem?

goodnews.h: Grammy winner Silvana Estrada joins the LA Phil
goodnews.b: Silvana Estrada, winner of this year's Latin Grammy for Best Singer-Songwriter Song, has been named the LA Phil's Creative Chair of Latin Music.
goodnews.title: Grammy-winning musician Silvana Estrada to program Latin music at the LA Phil

goodnews.h: Arcadia restorer revives Bob Hope's nativity set
goodnews.b: Sheila Lehman of La Porte Vintage in Arcadia, who specializes in restoring religious plaster statues, has been restoring a nativity set owned by the late Bob Hope.
goodnews.title: An Arcadia restorer is reviving Bob Hope’s nativity set — and looking for its missing angel

goodnews.h: Teen music nonprofit opens a permanent venue in Pasadena
goodnews.b: Backyard Party, which spent the past year moving from venue to venue staging shows for young bands, opened its permanent home in a northwest Pasadena warehouse.
goodnews.title: Born after the Eaton Fire, Backyard Party opens a permanent music venue for teens in Pasadena

local.h: Homeless man charged with murder in Chinatown killing
local.b: Police charged a homeless man with murder after a 62-year-old woman was found dead with signs of trauma to her neck at her Catherine Street apartment on Friday.
local.title: NYPD charges homeless man with murder after woman, 62, was killed at Chinatown apartment

local.h: FDNY leaders on lithium-ion fires and EMS shortages
local.b: Fire deaths have nearly doubled since last year, many driven by lithium-ion batteries, and EMS response times remain at a record high. FDNY Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore discussed the department's response on WNYC.
local.title: FDNY grapples with lithium-ion danger, EMS shortages and a building collapse

local.h: National Grid gas rate freeze approved, but costs may follow
local.b: State regulators approved a yearlong rate freeze for nearly 2 million National Grid gas customers in the city and on Long Island, but customers will still be on the hook for capital spending during the freeze.
local.title: New York approves National Grid rate freeze, but customers could see higher bills soon

local.h: Judge keeps man shot by ICE in the Bronx in custody
local.b: A federal judge ruled Oscar Belgal, wounded when federal agents fired on his SUV in the Bronx in October, will stay in custody while the administration pursues his deportation.
local.title: Federal judge in NY denies release of man shot by ICE in the Bronx

local.h: Rain returns Sunday, and another storm may hit Thanksgiving
local.b: Showers arrive Sunday afternoon and may linger into the Monday commute, with an inch or two of rain expected across the city. Forecasters are already watching a second storm near Thanksgiving.
local.title: Rain once again coming for NYC's idyllic fall — and maybe Thanksgiving, too

local.h: ICE arrest in Sea-Tac jetway draws Ferguson's rebuke

local.h: Popular-vote compact could near a key milestone
local.b: Next year Democrats will fully control five states that could join the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact, which awards electoral votes to the national popular-vote winner. Hurdles remain.
